content: Is there any objection if I start to think about PRs that contribute various sorting implementations + proofs of their correctness (plus build on what is in Mathlib etc. already). I know questions like complexity etc. are unresolved but I would quite like there to just exist some of the elementary content in this area.
There are already PRs in the algorithms side
I already have the comparison sort lower bound
Someone have also PRed stability proofs to my mergeSort and insertion Sort.
Great! But nothing actually in yet? What are the PRs?
Are the mergesort and insertion sort you have different to that in core and Mathlib?
CSLib#372 cslib#442 cslib#446
I am currently writing deterministic and randomised quicksort, but in Algolean
Insertion sort does. Merge sort matches what was written for TimeM to give reviewers a basis for comparison.
In fact for insertion sort iirc I proved that my program evaluates identically to the mathlib insertion sort to get correctness proofs for free

Right. I have to say I was not thinking about duplicating existing implementations or layering on this monadic model stuff - lower level really. I think there isn't much appetite for any sorting content in mathlib but this isn't really an approach I would like to follow.
One think that is unfinished in core is proof of correctness of their docs#Array.qsort
Indeed. I would like to do this here with the hope of getting it upstreamed - people haven't seemed very interested in it before but maybe if it exists...
I would also like a general predicate for "this sorting algorithm is correct" - quite a lot of theorems about mergesort and insertionsort are really just "this is a correct sort, and so..."

The thing is once you write the monadic program, you also get the pure lean function from it.

Having said that, you might want to see our Complexity folder which has generic definitions of a problem, its correctness and so on.

Fwiw a sorting algorithm has two properties for correctness :

  1. The output is a permutation of the input.
  2. The output is sorted.

I think both these properties are already defined for lists (Perm and Sorted which I believe you added). So I wonder if adding them into a structure helps?
SortedLE I added (Sorted was bad for various reasons and I killed it). Yes I am not sure if adding these as a structure helps - it might be a useful abbreviation.

In particular you want to be able to say, concisely "if X and Y are both sorted versions of a list L, then X = Y", which is not hard (we have all the necessary stuff for it), but to state it you have to invoke Perm.trans every time.
So I can see reasons why a short form is desirable!

(SortedLE btw is just a special case version of Pairwise really. Arguably what you really want to do is state stuff using Pairwise! Sorted used to be another name for Pairwise, which just made a lot of stuff a headache.)

On the other hand you might want to just go "we have some linear order", because in some cases (e.g. sorting networks which is closer to my direct area of expertise) you want to be able to succintly say "this sorts lists ascending" and "this sorts descending" which "SortedLE" and "SortedGE" provide (there are also SortedLT and SortedGT which are exactly what they sound like).
You might also want to say "This sorting algorithm works *on this class of inputs."
Fwiw, if you wish to make a pr to Algolean I’ll gladly review and merge it.
It already has two sorting algorithms so it might be a nice test bed for these definitions and how they might integrate into sorting algorithms.
